base_override.reason: Tempus files its weighted-average diluted share counts at a thousands scale (174,264 for FY2025) and the engine read them as units, inflating the magnitude of OE/share exactly 1,000x (the 5.4 run printed a market_cap_est of $11,278,366.08 against a $64.72 price). Engine 5.5 (2026-10-19): the unpinned preliminary run raised DATA_GAP:shares — SHARE_SCALE (base OE/share -3,932.44 is 60x the price, limit 20x) and emitted no tier; this declaration is the qualifying pin (no basis, value equal to the --base-oe-ps pin, the pin itself within 20x the price), so the final run carries the base as SHARE_SCALE_SUSPECT and prices the market cap on the latest diluted count x 1000 (174,264,000 shares, $11.440B in key_numbers.md). Every OE total leg (OCF, capex, SBC) is filed in dollars, and all three median years (FY2023-2025: 63,306 / 119,849 / 174,264) carry the same thousands scale, so dividing the engine's normalized base by 1,000 corrects it exactly. A shares_override cannot fix this: overrides fill only absent periods and never replace filed values. The correction changes no sign: the corrected base is still negative, so the name is Tier F, the tier the 5.4 run also printed on the uncorrected base; under engine 5.5 the unpinned run emits no tier at all (the share-scale gap), so the published Tier F now rests on this declared pin.
base_override.source: This run's dcf_numbers.json base_oe_normalized_per_share (-$3,932.4392632609865) divided by 1,000. Filing proof the diluted share counts are thousands-scaled: FY2025 diluted EPS as filed is -$1.41 (statements.json income) on net income of -$245,028,000 (financials_history.csv), which only reconciles at ~174 million shares, not 174,264; the Q3 2025 10-Q cover reports 172,863,470 Class A + 5,043,789 Class B shares outstanding at October 30, 2025; Q2 2026 weighted-average basic shares print 179,917 in the filing's thousands presentation against ~182.4 million shares outstanding at June 30, 2026.

moat_against: No demonstrated returns on capital: conservative owner's earnings positive in 0 of the last 4 filed years and negative on TTM through Q2 2026; operating losses every year; the roic_proxy series in fundamentals.json (+14.6% FY2022, +10.0% FY2023, +191.8% FY2024, +176.1% FY2025) is denominator noise on negative-then-thin equity with blank debt tags, not evidence of returns above the cost of capital
Diagnostics concentration: $955,381,000 of FY2025 revenue (75.1% in segments.json), oncology-centric; Data and applications is only $316,408,000

SBC is heavy and rising again: $124,747,000 in FY2025 after the $534,138,000 IPO year, $186,145,000 TTM through Q2 2026 (ttm.json) — a recurring tax on owners that alone exceeds TTM free cash flow in magnitude
Competition on every layer: Guardant Health and Natera in diagnostics, Flatiron Health (Roche) in oncology data, Illumina in sequencing, plus hospital/EHR platforms that own the workflow
Reimbursement and FDA-clearance dependence: the guided pricing uplift rests on ADLT pricing for xT CDx and an xF approval expected in late 2027 — regulatory outcomes, not contracted revenue
moat_for: One of the largest libraries of clinical and molecular oncology data in the world (FY2025 10-K, Item 1, quoted in profile.json) — multimodal data paired with clinical outcomes that compounds with every test run
Data flywheel monetized, not just claimed: Data and applications revenue $316,408,000 in FY2025, +30.9% YoY (segments.json), with data licensing / Insights the recurring, higher-value layer

Embedded clinical workflow and distribution: partnerships with 2,500+ healthcare institutions including 65% of U.S. academic medical centers and over 50% of U.S. oncologists (company descriptions in search results, 2026)
Diagnostics scale with regulatory assets: Diagnostics revenue $955,381,000 in FY2025 (segments.json); FDA-cleared xT CDx companion diagnostic carrying ADLT pricing
moat_justification: A real but unproven data moat: one of the largest clinical-plus-molecular oncology data libraries, a diagnostics business that feeds it, and a data-licensing layer growing +30.9% in FY2025 — set against zero years of positive owner's earnings, operating losses in every filed year, and no measurable return on capital through a cycle. Evidence first, per spec: the roic_proxy series in fundamentals.json is not usable evidence FOR a moat — it prints +191.8% (FY2024) and +176.1% (FY2025) while operating income was -$691,082,000 and -$252,872,000, because book equity was negative before the IPO (-$1,382,163,000 at FY2023) and thin after it, and the engine's debt tags are blank. The gross-margin series in fundamentals.json is null for every year (no COGS/gross-profit tag captured), so no five-year margin trend can be quoted from the computed outputs; the Q2 2026 earnings release (search-cited) prints gross profit of $246.5 million on revenue of $382.5 million. A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years.
